summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in probability theory, including Kolmogorov axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' Rule, and the properties of random variables. They further detail joint distributions, marginal densities, expectation, variance, and the law of iterated expectations.

summary: This document provides a comprehensive review of linear algebra topics including linear systems, rank, null space, linear maps, and diagonalization. It includes mini-lectures, practice problems, and detailed handwritten solutions for each section.

title: Linear Algebra: Guided Review and Exercises
summary: This document provides a comprehensive review of linear algebra topics, including solving linear systems, rank-nullity, linear maps, and diagonalization. It combines mini-lectures with worked examples and practice problems, including proofs and computational exercises.

summary: This document contains a comprehensive collection of 42 practice problems covering linear algebra, topology, differential calculus, and optimization theory. It is designed for independent study and includes theoretical proofs, computational exercises, and conceptual diagnostic questions.

It includes detailed, step-by-step solutions for several of the problems, particularly those involving the discrete metric and metric space properties.

summary: This document contains a collection of practice problems covering multivariate calculus (homogeneity, concavity, implicit function theorem, integration) and linear algebra (subspaces, linear independence, matrix rank, diagonalization). It includes some worked solutions for specific problems, particularly in the sections on partial derivatives and systems of linear equations.

summary: This document contains a set of advanced linear algebra exercises covering change of basis, inner product spaces, and idempotent matrices. It provides detailed step-by-step solutions for exercises on coordinate transformations, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, Cholesky decomposition, and properties of projection matrices.

summary: This document contains a set of linear algebra exercises covering column spaces, kernels, change of basis transformations, and inner product spaces. It includes problem statements followed by detailed solutions for each exercise.

title: Linear Algebra: Vector Spaces, Bases, and Linear Maps
summary: These notes provide a foundational overview of linear algebra, covering vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, and span. They further explain the concepts of basis, change of basis matrices, and the representation of linear maps as matrices between vector spaces.

title: Linear Algebra: Rank, Change of Basis, and Determinants
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including the Rank-Nullity Theorem, invariant subspaces, and the mechanics of changing bases for linear transformations. The document also explores the distinction between matrix equivalence and similarity, the properties of direct sums of subspaces, and the geometric interpretation of determinants.

title: Linear Algebra: Invariant Subspaces, Eigenvalues, and Inner Product Spaces
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including invariant subspaces, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and the process of diagonalization. The document also introduces inner product spaces, defining norms, orthogonality, and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

title: Linear Algebra: Spectral Theorem and Quadratic Forms
summary: These notes cover advanced linear algebra topics including the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the Gram-Schmidt process for orthonormal bases, and the Spectral Theorem for real symmetric matrices. It further explores the application of the Spectral Theorem to quadratic forms and the use of principal minor criteria to determine matrix definiteness.

summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in real analysis within Euclidean spaces, including sequence convergence, point-set topology (open/closed sets, compactness), and the continuity of mappings. summary: This is a comprehensive mathematics textbook focused on abstract vector spaces and linear maps, intended for students who have had a previous introductory exposure to the subject. It emphasizes deep conceptual understanding through rigorous definitions, theorems, and proofs, notably avoiding the use of determinants until the final chapters.

title: Book of Proof
summary: This textbook provides a comprehensive introduction to mathematical proof techniques, covering fundamental topics such as set theory, logic, counting, and various methods of proof including induction and contradiction. It is designed for undergraduate mathematics students to transition from computational mathematics to rigorous proof-based reasoning.

title: Principles of Mathematical Analysis
summary: This is a classic undergraduate-level textbook on real analysis by Walter Rudin. It covers fundamental topics including the real and complex number systems, topology, sequences and series, differentiation, integration, and the Lebesgue theory.

title: Mathematics for Economists
summary: This document is the table of contents and introductory material for a comprehensive textbook on mathematical methods used in economic theory. It covers foundational topics including one-variable calculus, linear algebra, and the calculus of several variables, with specific applications to economic models.

title: Essential Mathematics for Economic Analysis
summary: This document is the front matter and table of contents for the fourth edition of a comprehensive mathematics textbook designed for economics students. It outlines the foundational algebraic, functional, and logical topics covered in the text, ranging from basic arithmetic to advanced mathematical modeling.

title: Analysis in Euclidean Spaces
summary: This document provides a comprehensive introduction to analysis in Euclidean spaces, covering real number completeness, topology, continuity, differentiation, and integration. It is designed for PhD-level mathematics preparation, focusing on the analytical foundations required for economic modeling.

title: Optimization, Convexity and Correspondences
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of mathematical optimization techniques, covering convex geometry, convex and concave functions, and optimization in Euclidean space. It further explores equality and inequality-constrained optimization, duality, parameterized optimization, and fixed-point theorems, with specific applications to economic theory.

title: Part IV: Probability Theory
summary: These lecture notes provide a comprehensive overview of probability theory, covering both computational and measure-theoretic perspectives. The document progresses from basic probability spaces and random variables to expectation, conditional expectation, stochastic convergence, and limit theorems, with specific applications to econometrics.
